document.title: Phase 7: Deferred features
document.p: Goal (PLAN.md, ): everything left out of Phases 2 to 4 except schema awareness (Phase 5): full UCA collations, fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc, Invisible XML, XSLT streaming, the XQuery Update Facility, Full Text, EXPath Binary and File, XPath 1.0 compatibility mode and XSLT backwards-compatible behaviour, a timezone database, other calendars and languages in the formatting functions, and fn:transform. The owner has said every deferred feature must be supported eventually (). Four features no phase covers yet are proposed below for the owner. Design: . Rules for parallel packets are those of docs/tasks/phase-2.md (, , : a packet starts when every packet in its "After" list is committed), plus the shared-table rule below. Phase 7 must not regress the counts of Phases 2 to 5.

item.p: Each feature replaces its one rejection place (). Every packet below names the place where sxml rejects or ignores the feature today, with the error the specification gives a processor without it. The packet replaces that place. It does not add a second path beside it. When the feature is in, the packet also removes the feature from the drivers' non-goal lists (tests/qt4/driver/applicability.c, tests/xslt/driver/xslt_applicability.c) and sets its system property (src/system_property.c).
One IR, one evaluator, one tree builder. No feature adds an evaluator or a tree kind:
Dynamic evaluation (xsl:evaluate) and fn:transform compile at run time and ask the machine for a unit evaluation, as fn:load-xquery-module does (glossary , ).
Parsers for other notations (HTML5, Invisible XML, DTD-driven entities, XML 1.1) send tree builder events (tree.h), as the XML parser does. The result is an ordinary arena tree.
DTD validation is schema validation. The DTD's declarations become schema components (src/schema_internal.h), and the validator (a tree builder filter, ) checks them.
Updates do not change trees. A pending update list is applied by copying the affected trees through the tree builder with the changes made, so tree.h stays frozen ().
Streaming consumes the parser's builder events as a receiving task (). Before that, streamability analysis is a static pass over the XSLT AST.
Full Text compiles a selection into a match program, as the regex engine compiles a pattern (). The program is run by a loop, not by recursion ().
No substrate change is planned. , view, memory, , name, types, , xdm and export stay as they are. The planned header changes are additive and each needs a decision record:
processor.h: optional features (7.2), a file-system interface (7.9) and new resource kinds (7.10, 7.12, 7.15, 7.16, 7.18);
xpath.h: the XPath 1.0 compatibility flag (7.4);
xquery.h: updating queries (7.7);
xml.h: DTD options (7.14).

Size (below): sxml.wasm is 1,998,723 of 2,000,000 bytes. Every feature that XPath can reach would link into it. Packet carries out the owner's choice, and features that would grow sxml.wasm wait for 7.2.

section.p: In total these features would unlock about 4,400 of XQ40's 5,505 not-run cases, about 3,330 of XT40's 4,659, and 540 xmlconf cases. Other not-run features are not planned. They are listed so the owner sees them: staticTyping (77 XQ40, 48 XP40), xsl-stylesheet-processing-instruction (23 XT40), HTML4 output (3), schema-location-hint (3), XInclude (2), and remote_http (2).

When a packet lands, its cases enter the denominators. A feature that passes below the current rate lowers XP40's, XQ40's or XT40's gate rate even though no pass is lost. This is why each feature has a gate of its own, below.

section.title: Size: optional build parts (owner decision, Proposed)
section.p: The JavaScript package links XPath only, so the following features cost nothing in sxml.wasm: XSLT- and XQuery-only features (streaming, the Update Facility, Full Text in the XQuery grammar, xsl:evaluate, disable-output-escaping, XSLT backwards compatibility). They do grow the sxml CLI module, which is 4,877,565 of 5,500,000 bytes. The other features are reachable from XPath and would link into sxml.wasm. The estimates below (to be measured by 7.2) are of stripped bytes. Measured references: linking XSLT added 1,159,058 bytes to the CLI module (), and linking schema validation added 268,168 bytes ().

section.p: If every XPath-reachable feature were linked, sxml.wasm would grow by about 0.5 to 0.8 MB, to about 2.6 MB. The options:

item.p: Raise the budget per feature as it lands. This costs no code. Every browser user downloads every table, used or not, and the budget ends near 2.8 MB stripped (about 0.9 MB gzipped).

Optional features chosen at link time (recommended, with 4). One public mechanism: the processor configuration takes a view of sxml_optional_feature values (processor.h, additive, a record). Each feature has an exported function that returns one, for example sxml_uca_collation_feature(), sxml_html_parser_feature() or sxml_xslt_transform_feature(). The core reaches a feature only through that value's operations table. Without the value, the feature's place stays the behaviour (FOCH0002, XPST0017, FODT0004), so a program that never names a feature does not link it.
What stays the same: one build, every feature tested in every build, and no #if.
The JavaScript package ships sxml.wasm as today, plus a larger module (or a few) that names the features. Its API takes a feature list.
Costs: one processor.h addition; an operations table per feature (about 1 KB each); behaviour that depends on the host's configuration (the drivers and the CLI name every feature).
The core still needs headroom for core changes (DTD, XML 1.1, the compatibility mode). The proposal is 2,100,000 bytes for the core and 3,000,000 for the full module.
CMake options (SXML_WITH_UCA and similar). At compile time, stub files hold the rejection places in place of the excluded sources.
Advantage: no header change.
Costs: at least two configurations to build and test (minimal and full); a binary's features are fixed when it is built; and two sxml binaries of one version behave differently.
Large data as host resources (adds to 2 or 3). sxml compiles in readers for standard formats, and the host supplies the data through the resource resolver:
DUCET as allkeys.txt (UTS #10 format) and tailorings as CLDR rule text (UTS #35, Part 5);
the timezone database as TZif files (RFC 8536): the CLI reads /usr/share/zoneinfo, and the JavaScript package fetches files on demand.
A compiled built-in copy can be its own optional feature, for hosts that want no files. Costs:
new resource kinds (processor.h, additive);
parsing at first use (allkeys.txt is 1.9 MB of text; loading it takes an estimated 20 to 60 ms);
correctness that depends on the version of the host's data (tests pin it);
no help for features that are mostly code (HTML5, iXML, Binary).

Shared tables. Each packet changes only its own entries in the drivers' dependency and non-goal tables and in src/system_property.c, as single hunks staged ledger-style (BRIEF.md). The CLI grows only when a feature works (BRIEF.md, ).

section.title: Packets
section.p: Each packet gives: the specifications; the cases it unlocks; the rejection place it replaces and the mechanism it extends; header changes; dependencies ("After"); what it owns; size; and its gate (proposed, for the owner). "Owns" lists new files, plus the existing files the packet changes beyond single shared-table entries.

section.p: No phase covers these four features yet ( Proposed).
